Iranian F-5 pilots recounted the March 1 airstrikes on the U.S. Camp Buehring in Kuwait.
According to their account, they were aware of the presence of Patriot batteries, layered air defenses, AWACS coverage, and Kuwaiti F/A-18s. To avoid detection, they maintained complete radio silence and flew at extremely low altitude over the Gulf, less than 50 feet above the water, far below the standard 500-foot training profile. One pilot claimed the aircraft even passed between two ships whose decks stood higher than the jet itself.
After entering Kuwaiti airspace, they bypassed other potential targets, including power lines and refineries, and proceeded directly toward Camp Buehring, maintaining high speed and very low altitude until reaching the target area.
The pilots stated that the strike caused major fires and multiple secondary explosions, including burning helicopters.

Iran’s Red Crescent Society (IRCS) has signed a memorandum of understanding with Russia to acquire 20 Mi-171 helicopters for emergency response and disaster relief.
The helicopters will be used for search and rescue, medical evacuation, firefighting, and other emergency operations.
They are expected to be equipped with modern systems, including night-vision capability and specialized medical equipment. The first four helicopters are scheduled for delivery before March 2027.

Footage from the 40-Day War shows the moment the warhead separates from an Iranian Ghadr-M (Qadr-M) ballistic missile over the skies of Israel.
Iran used a liquid-fueled Ghadr missile for the first time equipped with three separable, maneuverable warheads. Each Qadr-M warhead, weighing around 200–250 kg, could reportedly guide itself after separation and hit different targets.
This appears to be Iran’s first known use of Multiple Independently Targetable Reentry Vehicles (MIRVs). The capability is likely still at an early stage, but if further developed, it could significantly complicate air defense operations.

Lockheed Martin has unveiled a new version of the M142 HIMARS multiple launch rocket system (MLRS) called HIMARS FLEX.
The rocket system is now even more modular and multifunctional, while also receiving a doubled ammunition load comparable to that of the M270. Instead of a single launch pod carrying 6 GMLRS/ER GMLRS rockets, 1 ATACMS missile, or 2 PrSM missiles, the HIMARS FLEX carries two launch pods.
In addition, beyond its role as a launcher for tactical ballistic missiles and rockets, the HIMARS FLEX can also serve as a launcher for 8 Patriot PAC-3 surface-to-air missiles.

The Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) will release a short documentary with firsthand accounts from F-5 Air Force pilots involved in the surprise operation targeting the U.S. Camp Buehring in Kuwait.

Hezbollah released footage showing the targeting of IDF equipment, including an M109 Doher self-propelled howitzer, two Humvees, and a Namer armored personnel carrier (APC) in southern Lebanon, using Ababil fiber-optic FPV drones.
The IRGC has carried out a drone strike on the headquarters of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups near Koy Sanjaq, east of Erbil in northern Iraq, using multiple Shahed-136 one-way attack drones.

Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters has issued a stern warning to Israel, stating that the IDF violated the ceasefire 84 times over the past two days following President Trump's announcement of the end of the war. The statement added that if Israel does not cease its actions in southern Lebanon, it should expect a severe response from the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran.
Hezbollah released footage dated May 29, 2026, showing the targeting of an IDF soldier in the settlement of Misgav Am in northern Israel using an Ababil fiber-optic FPV drone.
